test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two classes took the same test. One class of 20 students made an average grade of 85%, the other class of 30 students made an average grade of 70%. The average grade for all students across both classes is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of students in **Class 1** and **Class 2** = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.

Using the **Deviation Method**: Let the assumed average be 70%.

Deviation for Class 1 = (85% − 70%) = +15% per student.

Net deviation for 2 units = 2 × 15% = +30%.

Distribute net deviation over total ratio parts (2 + 3 = 5): 30% ÷ 5 = 6%.

Final average = Assumed average + deviation = 70% + 6% = 76%.

**∴ The correct answer is 76%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in **Class A** (n₁) = 20 | Average grade (A₁) = 85%

Number of students in **Class B** (n₂) = 30 | Average grade (A₂) = 70%

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = [(n₁ × A₁) + (n₂ × A₂)] ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad3855b7f409d1957821bfcdcdd6c7abc81be49fd97d344d3c0b6245c5ed2669.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of grades for Class A = 20 × 85 = 1700

⇒ Total sum of grades for Class B = 30 × 70 = 2100

⇒ Total sum of grades for both classes = 1700 + 2100 = 3800

⇒ Total number of students = 20 + 30 = 50

⇒ **Average grade** for all students = 3800 ÷ 50

⇒ Combined Average = 76%

**∴ The correct answer is 76%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

When two groups with different averages are combined, the **resultant average** lies closer to the average of the larger group (in this case, 70% because Class 2 has 30 students).

Ratio and Alligation

The difference between the averages and the mean is **inversely proportional** to the number of students: (85 − 76) : (76 − 70) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2, which matches the student ratio 30 : 20.

General Formula for n Groups

Weighted Average = (∑nᵢAᵢ) ÷ ∑nᵢ, where n is the number of items and A is the value of each item.</p
